importance_ranking.reason: Buyers scan listing images to confirm wooden construction (vs MS/FRP/PUF alternatives) and assess build quality, size scale, and finish before reading any text. Visual sub-type variation across sizes, wall finishes, and roof types is significant — wrong material or scale triggers an immediate skip.

Cabin size is non-interchangeable and is the primary shortlisting gate — a buyer with a fixed gate footprint cannot substitute one size for another. Wall material and insulation type drive price and durability fit; listings without these specs cannot be evaluated.

Indian buyers in this segment — construction contractors, society committees, facility managers — are highly price-sensitive and compare prices across sellers once size is confirmed. Price varies substantially with cabin size and material grade, making it a primary shortlisting lever after spec match.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant brand with buyer recall exists in this category — the market is fragmented across regional fabricators and local manufacturers; buyers search by size and price, not manufacturer name.
importance_ranking.reason: Buyers prefer a local manufacturer who can deliver and install on-site; seller location, manufacturing capability, and delivery track record matter moderately during vendor selection but do not gate initial engagement.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Some manufacturers quote per sq ft for custom-dimension builds, but per piece is the universal dominant unit for complete cabin transactions. No buyer questions the unit for a finished cabin.
importance_ranking.reason: A wooden guard room is a complete, self-contained cabin unit — per piece is the only conceivable quoting unit and is never a source of buyer confusion.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Cabin size is non-interchangeable across buyer requirements and is the single largest price driver — a 4x4 ft cabin and a 10x8 ft cabin serve entirely different site constraints and cannot be substituted.
Wood type defines the material quality tier — plywood vs teak wood vs hardwood represents a significant price delta and durability difference that buyers cannot substitute across.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Marine ply (BWP/BWR grade) vs blockboard vs cement fibre board vs MDF is a primary quality and durability differentiator that buyers use to compare cabins — panel grade determines weather resistance and longevity, and is not captured by Wood Type (species) or Wall Finish (surface treatment).

Buyers in hot or cold climates specify insulation requirement before purchase — an insulated PUF panel cabin costs significantly more than a basic uninsulated unit, and sellers need this to quote accurately; the current 'Features' spec captures insulation only as a binary flag without specifying type.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Cabin size is non-interchangeable — a seller stocking only 4x4 ft units cannot supply an 8x6 ft order, making size the primary routing spec that determines which sellers can respond.

Wood type places the buyer in a specific price and quality tier — a buyer specifying teak wood vs plywood panel is in a different budget segment, enabling sellers to quote accurately and avoid mismatched responses.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Sellers need to know whether the buyer requires insulation to confirm product fit and quote accurately — an insulated PUF or thermocol cabin is a structurally different and significantly more expensive product than a basic uninsulated wooden cabin.
